findings.title: Failed MR creation leaves the revert branch behind, and the fixed branch name blocks every retry
findings.body: The branch is named `revert-<first 8 of sha>` (line 970), so it is the same on every attempt. Only the `/revert` call has cleanup (lines 972-982). If the revert commit is pushed and the `merge_requests` POST at line 983 then fails (permissions, an MR already open for that source branch, a network error, a timeout), the branch with the revert commit stays on the project. The next click then fails at line 971 because the branch already exists, with no hint why. The user has to delete the branch by hand. Reverting twice in a row hits the same error. Either also delete the branch when the MR creation fails, or reuse or suffix the branch name so a retry can proceed. The cleanup comment at line 973 already treats an orphan branch as unwanted.

findings.title: The no-commit error path and a failing MR creation are not covered
findings.body: The two new tests cover the happy path and a failing `/revert` call. The `GitLabRevertUnavailableError` path (`merge_commit_sha` and `squash_commit_sha` both null, GitLabPullRequestCli.ts:963) has no test, and neither does a failure at the final `merge_requests` POST. The first of these is a new user-visible error and the second is where the orphan-branch behavior comes from. A row in the existing revert test, or a short second case, would settle both.

contracts.action: Revert a merged GitLab merge request: read the MR, create branch revert-<sha8> from the target branch, POST the commit revert onto it, open a new MR
contracts.equivalent_path: GitHub's revert in packages/source-control-github/src/server/GitHubPullRequestApi.ts:2459 is a single RevertPullRequest GraphQL mutation. It creates the branch and the PR atomically on the host, so it has no partial state. GitLab has no equivalent endpoint, so this is four separate REST writes.
contracts.before_after: Before: GitLab 'revert' was in actionArgs' unsupported list and was not advertised. After: the action is advertised in definition.ts:59 and gated on viewerCanMerge (Provider.ts:62), and runMergeRequestAction dispatches to revertMergeRequest (Cli.ts:1743). The provider wraps runAction in `writing`, which invalidates the detail cache before and after (Provider.ts:437, 142-158). The web UI shows the button only when detail.state === 'merged' (PullRequestActionsMenu.tsx:442), and mobile also gates on merged (pullRequestActions.ts:96).
contracts.visible_effect: On success the web UI toasts 'Revert merge request opened' (PullRequestDetailPanel.tsx:690-691) and refreshes. On failure it toasts the 'Could not open a revert ...' label with a hint (PullRequestDetailPanel.tsx:170, 189).
contracts.failure_mode: A failure at read, branch creation or revert is visible as a toast. A revert conflict deletes the branch (Cli.ts:972-982). A failure at the final MR POST leaves the revert branch on the project, and retries then fail at branch creation because the name is fixed. The server does not check that the MR is merged. A non-merged MR would get the 'landed as several commits' message, which would be misleading, but the UI gates this.

summary: The GitLab revert is a sound four-step REST flow. It is gated on merge permission and on merged state in both clients, and it cleans up the branch when the revert itself fails. One gap: if opening the revert MR fails, the fixed-name branch is left behind and blocks every retry. The new tests also skip the null-commit error path and the failing MR creation.
